facts.fact: The World Bank says 100 percent of Takaful and Karama beneficiaries are paid through electronic means, via Meeza debit cards, as of December 2023.

Egypt's unified government services card system is being rolled out in phases, with phase one in Port Said, phase two in Ismailia and Luxor and phase three planned for the remaining governorates, as reported to the Prime Minister.

The unified card system serves health insurance, food subsidy, Takaful and Karama pension and subsidised fertilizer through one card, with 41,500 ration families in Port Said, per the Prime Minister's meeting.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Social Solidarity said Takaful and Karama beneficiaries, 4.7 million families, receive June 2026 payments electronically through bank ATMs, Nasser Social Bank branches, Fawry outlets and the programme's Meeza cards.

Takaful and Karama pensions are sent monthly to beneficiaries' mobile wallets once a social unit enters the request on the system and links the pension to the wallet, per the Ministry of Social Solidarity as reported.

facts.fact: Ministry undersecretary Ahmed Abdelrahman said the ministry has fully redeveloped the Takaful and Karama system as an integrated digital system, with social researchers recording field data on tablets instead of paper forms.

Minister Maya Morsy told parliament's plan and budget committee that, after 10 years, Takaful and Karama has integrated databases and a network link from its database to more than 20 state bodies, reaching about 4.7 million families.

Egypt's Ministry of Social Solidarity says Takaful and Karama applicants are recorded by field researchers on tablets or computers with scanned documents, reviewed by the social unit head and sent to a central database for verification and eligibility testing.
